messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Ibuprofen can increase your risk of fatal heart attack, heart failure, or stroke.
Do not use Ibuprofen just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking ibuprofen after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
Ibuprofen may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using Ibuprofen, especially in older adults.
Do not take more than your recommended dose.
An ibuprofen overdose can damage your stomach or intestines.
Use only the smallest amount of medication needed to get relief from your pain, swelling, or fever.
Triplet: ["ibuprofen", "has overdose effect", "damage to stomach or intestines"]

The relation 'has overdose effect' in the triplet is defined as 'An overdose of the subject drug can cause the adverse effect specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has overdose symptom': An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
B. 'has overdose risk': An overdose of the subject drug may result in the serious or life-threatening consequence specified by the object entity.
C. 'has side effect': The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
D. 'has side effect location': The adverse effect caused by the subject drug occurs at the location specified by the object entity.
E. 'has serious side effect': The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
